evidence: The report at creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md:65-69 recommends papers at the study level. The controlling creativity-codebook.md, section 3 (lines 30-34), requires random assignment to AI assistance, at least 50 participants, and output-scored creativity or diversity. Form-spec.md:144 explicitly applies these criteria to at least one study; it does not require a published full-arm intention-to-treat estimate. I opened Abdulhai et al (2026) - How LLMs Distort Our Written Language.pdf from the pdf_path in retrieval.json. PDF p. 4, section 3.1, explicitly reports random assignment of 100 people to no LLM (45) or embedded gpt-4o-mini access (55). PDF p. 22, sections A.3-A.4, instructs each participant to write an essay. PDF p. 8, Figure 4b, and pp. 8-9, section 4.2, compute embeddings of the completed essays and compare their spread across writers, providing an output-based diversity outcome. I also independently inspected p. 8's PDF vector stream: Figure 4b XObject 1429 has 43 /M0 Do, 29 /M1 Do, and 27 /M2 Do marker calls, supporting an essay analysis above the 50-person threshold without relying on the unresolved overall analyzed N. The finding correctly describes p. 5's actual-use classification and pp. 8-9's subgroup comparisons; these contrasts are not randomized by use intensity. It also correctly identifies creativity as self-report (pp. 8 and 24) and the archived-draft revision study as AI-versus-human output (pp. 5-6). However, those observations do not negate S1's study-level eligibility under the stated rules. The report already discloses nonrandom use intensity and the selected subgroup at lines 156-157, and requests a full randomized-arm diversity effect at line 160. The form likewise distinguishes these limitations from paper eligibility. Form-spec.md:140 permits figure_only statistics. Codebook section 4 classifies estimates, while section 3 and form-spec.md:144 determine study eligibility; the subgroup estimates cannot be interpreted as randomized effects, but the auditor adds an unstated requirement when using their reporting limitation to demote the entire paper. No change to eligibility.core or final.core is warranted for this finding; tools/build_report.py:90-104 correctly maps final.core=yes to status core.
